raw_case_text:
In June 2009, a 37-year-old man presented at our out-patient clinics with generalized multiple erythematous, pustular plaques, papules, and nodules preexisting since several years (Figure 1). In addition, in physical and laboratory examination, severe cachexia, pancytopenia, and hepatosplenomegaly were evident. The patient was known to be HIV positive for about 20 years, and in spite of long-term virological suppression, CD4 cells never exceeded 100 cells/muL. A skin biopsy revealed a dense infiltrate of histiocytic cells with Donovan bodies compatible with cutaneous leishmaniasis (Figure 2(a)). Leishmania serology was negative, but PCR from blood and skin samples was positive for L. donovani/infantum complex. In addition to cutaneous leishmaniasis, bone marrow aspiration showed infiltration with Leishmania confirming visceral leishmaniasis (Figure 2(b)). The patient reported yearly holiday trips to Ischia (Gulf of Naples) during prior decades.
Systemic first-line therapy with liposomal amphotericin B (iv, 4 mg/kg days 1-5, day 10, then 5 times in weekly intervals) was started. Since lower response rates to first-line therapy in HIV-infected patients are described, miltefosine (po, 100 mg/day) was added to the standard amphotericin B regimen. Initial response to treatment was adequate, the patient gained weight, the pancytopenia improved, CD4 cell count increased, and Leishmania PCR from blood was negative. HI-viral load was suppressed at any time point. Due to the poor CD4 response and the high relapse rate described in HIV-infected patients, the previous induction regime was followed by maintenance therapy with liposomal amphotericin B (iv, every 3 weeks) and miltefosine (po, 50 mg thrice weekly) planned to be administered until immune recovery (i.e., >350 CD4 cells/muL) has been repeatedly documented. Nevertheless, one year after the treatment initiation, Leishmania PCR from blood turned positive again. Thus, a second induction cycle of liposomal amphotericin and miltefosine (po, 100 mg/day) was started. In spite of clinical response to treatment, Leishmania PCR remained positive over the next six months. Therefore, miltefosine was stopped and replaced by interferon gamma (100 mug sc 3 times/week). Initial tolerance to interferon was good, but after 12 weeks, the patient developed severe leukopenia (1950/muL) and thrombopenia (24000/muL), and interferon gamma administrations had to be stopped. An extensive re-evaluation after 2 years after diagnosis and treatment start revealed Leishmania parasites in blood, bone marrow, gastric mucosa, and the biliary tract. Based on data reporting treatment approaches with pentamidine and the successful use fluconazole and allopurinol in patients with mucocutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis, we started a new therapy cycle combining pentamidine (iv, initial dose 4 mg/kg, then 3 mg/kg), fluconazole (po, 200 mg/day), and allopurinol (po, 300 mg/day) for 3 weeks followed by maintenance therapy with allopurinol and intravenous pentamidine every 3 weeks. Therapy with pentamidine was complicated by recurrent hypertensive crisis and two episodes of pulmonary edema requiring intensive care. Nevertheless, this treatment regime led to an instant and impressive recovery of hematopoiesis, a continuous rise of CD4 cells (absolute count and percentage), and last but not least to undetectability of Leishmania in peripheral blood and bone marrow.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 37-year-old HIV-positive male presented with generalized erythematous papules, pustular plaques, and nodules persisting for several years, accompanied by severe weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a multi-year history of generalized cutaneous eruptions comprising papules, pustular plaques, and nodules that progressively involved extensive body areas. Over this period, he experienced severe progressive wasting, weakness, and abdominal swelling. Despite sustained HIV viral suppression on antiretroviral therapy, his CD4 count had remained persistently below 100 cells/muL.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection diagnosed 20 years prior with profound cellular immunodeficiency (nadir and sustained CD4 <100 cells/muL) on long-term suppressive ART. Epidemiological exposure: annual vacations to Ischia (Gulf of Naples, Italy) over preceding decades.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports generalized cutaneous lesions, severe cachexia, profound fatigue, and abdominal fullness; denies acute fevers.

objective.physical_examination: Severe cachexia. Dermatologic examination revealed widespread generalized erythematous papules, pustular plaques, and subcutaneous nodules across the face, trunk, and extremities. Abdominal examination revealed marked hepatosplenomegaly.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count revealed pancytopenia. CD4 cell count: <100 cells/muL. HIV viral load: suppressed/undetectable. During subsequent interferon therapy, leukocyte count dropped to 1,950/muL and platelet count to 24,000/muL.
objective.advanced_workup: Skin punch biopsy: dense dermal histiocytic infiltration containing abundant intracellular Donovan bodies. Bone marrow aspirate: heavy intracellular protozoal infiltration with hemophagocytosis. Upper gastrointestinal and biliary endoscopy/biopsy (at 2-year relapse): demonstrated protozoal infiltration throughout the gastric mucosa and biliary tract.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: PCR assays from blood and cutaneous biopsies were positive for Leishmania donovani/infantum complex. Bone marrow aspirate demonstrated abundant Leishmania amastigotes, and histopathology of skin, gastric mucosa, and biliary tract confirmed disseminated cutaneous, visceral, and gastrointestinal leishmaniasis. Leishmania serology was false-negative due to severe immunosuppression. Management and Outcome: Initial induction with IV liposomal amphotericin B (4 mg/kg on days 1-5, 10, then weekly for 5 doses) combined with oral miltefosine (100 mg/day) achieved remission, followed by secondary prophylaxis (amphotericin B every 3 weeks plus miltefosine 50 mg three times weekly). Relapse occurred at 1 year, refractory to re-induction and adjunct interferon-gamma (complicated by severe cytopenias). A salvage combination of IV pentamidine (initial 4 mg/kg, then 3 mg/kg), oral fluconazole (200 mg/day), and oral allopurinol (300 mg/day) for 3 weeks followed by every-3-week pentamidine maintenance achieved durable parasitological cure and hematologic reconstitution, despite complications of hypertensive crises and pulmonary edema managed in the ICU.
